headline: Open-source tools standardize omics, peptide sequencing, and benchmarking workflows
label: Reproducible Bioinformatics Software Infrastructure
summary: Deep learning models and multi-omics pipelines are now distributed as containerized, reproducible, GUI-accessible software for routine use.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints and publications is the packaging of computational methods as accessible, reproducible software rather than new predictive models alone. CasanovoGUI wraps the Casanovo deep learning de novo peptide sequencing model in a cross-platform desktop application, while Cell-Hub and SMART deliver containerized R/Shiny and Dockerised pipelines for scRNA-seq and somatic variant interpretation. RomicsProcessor and EHItk emphasize FAIR principles and metadata-driven access to multi-omics and hologenome resources, and PathoBench provides a community registry of pathogen benchmark datasets with metrics. scRepresenter adds a workflow for computing and benchmarking cellular embeddings from foundation models. What is distinctive here is the treatment of evaluation and reproducibility as built-in features of the software. The items are heterogeneous; only a subset involves learned prediction.
